fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Entry Area; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Open Green Space
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Limited Turnaround Space; Dense Vegetation
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions of approach.
• Mark the single access point clearly so responding units can confirm they have reached the correct entry without delay.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach the front entry without obstruction.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the driveway so emergency vehicles can pass without branches blocking the path or cab visibility.
• Clear a designated turnaround area near the residence so emergency vehicles are not forced to back out to the street.
• Keep the turnaround area free of parked vehicles, equipment, and stored materials at all times.
• Cut back dense vegetation along walkways leading to the front entry so responders can move on foot without obstruction.
• Thin vegetation between the street and the front entry so the residence and front door are visible to arriving units from the access point.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Shrubs; Open Green Space; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Ground Vegetation; Irrigated Landscape
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or touch the house roofline and eaves.
• Remove dead leaves, twigs, and plant debris that have collected against the base of the house.
• Thin shrubs growing close to the house walls to create open space between the plants and the structure.
• Keep the ground vegetation immediately around the house mowed short and free of dry, dead material.
• Separate any shrubs that are growing into or touching the lower branches of nearby trees.
• Remove dead or dry plant material that has accumulated under shrubs near the house.
• Keep scattered trees near the house trimmed so their lower branches are lifted off the ground.
